stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is deciding how to package several daily medications for one patient. Which statements correctly apply the Schedule II/III rule? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A stable maintenance classification permits a Schedule II drug to share a multi-drug single-dose pouch.
A licensee may not dispense a Schedule II or III controlled substance in a multi-drug single-dose package.
That prohibition does not by its own terms ban a single-drug single-dose package.
Every form of compliance packaging is prohibited for every Schedule II or III controlled substance.
The policy phrase 'unless otherwise prohibited' preserves the regulatory Schedule II/III restriction.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b) prohibits a licensee from dispensing Schedule II or III controlled substances in a multi-drug-single-dose package. Maintenance status does not create an exception. The text is specific to multi-drug-single-dose packaging, so it must not be expanded into a ban on every form of compliance packaging. Current Policy 2023-01 begins its multi-drug section with 'Unless otherwise prohibited' and therefore preserves the regulation rather than overriding it.

choice_analysis.A: Maintenance status does not override 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b).
choice_analysis.B: Correct: this is the express Schedule II/III multi-drug-single-dose prohibition.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the cited clause is drawn by packaging type and does not itself reach single-drug-single-dose packaging.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the policy does not displace an otherwise applicable regulatory prohibition.

related_facts: Other compatibility, labeling, policy and procedure requirements continue to apply.
explanation.mpje_trap: Turning a precise multi-drug-single-dose prohibition into either a maintenance exception or a universal packaging ban.

reasoning_steps: Identify whether the proposed package is multi-drug-single-dose
Apply the prohibition without expanding it to a different packaging type
